success_patterns: First-turn flight requests with an origin and destination but no literal date ('one-way for 2 travelers', 'for my birthday', 'for a wedding', 'a specific arrival time') succeeded when the whole output was one short seek_information naming only the departure date. Flight + hotel with only a destination asked for the origin city, departure date, and hotel dates in one call.

When the assistant asked for dates and the user replied with a date range, the agent immediately ran search_hotels with the city from turn 1 and the party size and per-night budget from earlier turns, saved as 'hotels'. It did not ask again and did not filter.

A bare class reply ('I prefer first') with a single flight key in CACHE produced load, filter_flights(flight_class=[...]), save under a new key. Only the new constraint was passed. The arrival-time and date constraints already in the cache summary were not re-passed.
Seek_information was written without optional items (class, airline, passenger count, hotel dates for an unrequested hotel).

The one trajectory that wrote a placeholder date (departure_date=['<date>']) failed execution, though its cache comparison still matched. Literal dates only is the lesson. No literal date means seek_information.

patch.reasoning: All observed successes are already covered by existing rules, so no new gate is added. The optimizer notes say to remove contradictions instead of stacking text. Three fast-rule clauses conflict with the protected guidance, which says to pass only the last message's new constraint, to put a stated class in the flight search, and to use filter_attractions(city=...) for a city reply. The edits below remove those conflicts. They match the successful behaviour: filters carry only the new constraint, and searches carry the stated constraints.

edits.target: the constraints introduced in the LAST user turn, plus any earlier-stated constraint that the CACHE summary text ("Additionally filtering for ..." / search description) does not show as applied. Do NOT repeat filters or search parameters the summary already lists.
edits.content: only the constraints introduced in the LAST user turn. Everything said in earlier turns is already in the cached entry, so never re-pass it.

edits.target: Include an earlier-stated constraint only if the summary does NOT list it.
edits.content: Earlier-turn constraints are already in the entry, so pass only the last message's new constraint.

edits.target: Add no other params: no airline, flight_class, budget, times or num_people.
edits.content: Add no param the user did not state (never num_people, num_layovers or times). A class or airline the user did state goes into both searches.

edits.target: and do not add city to a filter.
edits.content: and do not add city to a hotel, restaurant or flight filter. The only exception is filter_attractions(city=...) when the user names a city for attractions cached at state level.
